context.testbed_question: When some agents in a coding swarm secretly collude, does a monitor catch the backdoors they ship past their own reviews?

context.idea_description: A backdoor is a shortcut: one small input change sends every image to the target class. Instead of Neural Cleanse's masked patch, search per class for the smallest single additive perturbation (L2 penalty, no mask) that flips most clean images to that class. A backdoored model should have one class reachable with an anomalously small universal perturbation, regardless of the trigger's shape, so the detector should transfer to trigger families it was not tuned on.
context.idea_title: Minimal universal perturbation as a backdoor detector
context.metric: AUROC, clean vs held-out-family models

context.idea_description: Do not train the strong student on the weak labels directly. First train an intermediate model on them, here a linear probe on the student's frozen backbone, which has too little capacity to memorize label noise. Then relabel the training data with the intermediate model's predictions and fine-tune the full student on those. Prediction: the student copies fewer of the weak supervisor's errors and recovers more of the gap.
context.metric: Performance gap recovered (PGR)

context.idea_description: Heavy-tailed self-regularization theory reads training history from the singular value spectra of weight matrices. Poisoning teaches a model one extra, very strong input-output rule, which should show up as an outlying top singular value relative to the bulk. Score each model by the ratio of the largest to the second-largest singular value across its layers. Needs no data at all.
